      "text": "Vision Statement: Continue Coral Gables vision and mission as a community that is attractive to live, \nwork, play and visit.",

    },

    {
      "section_id": "s0030",
      "heading_path": [
        "Future Land Use Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal FLU-1."
      ],
      "page_start": 5,
      "page_end": 5,
      "text": "Protect, strengthen, and enhance the City of Coral Gables as a vibrant community ensuring that its \nneighborhoods, business opportunities, shopping, employment centers, cultural activities, historic \nvalue, desirable housing, open spaces, and natural resources make the City a very desirable place to \nwork, live and play.",
      "tables": []
    },

      "section_id": "s0031",
      "heading_path": [
        "Future Land Use Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal FLU-1.",
        "Objective FLU-1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 5,
      "page_end": 5,
      "text": "Preserve Coral Gables as a “placemaker” where the balance of existing and future uses is \nmaintained to achieve a high quality living environment by encouraging compatible land uses, \nrestoring and protecting the natural environment, and providing facilities and services which meet \nor exceed the minimum Level of Service (LOS) standards and meet the social and economic needs \nof the community through the Comprehensive Plan and Future Land Use Classifications and Map \n(see FLU-1: Future Land Use Map).",
      "tables": []
    },

      "page_end": 5,

      "text": "Pursuant to Section 163.3177(5), F.S. as amended, the City hereby adopts the following planning \nperiods: from 2025 to 2035; and 2025 to 2045. \n(Ord. No. 2025-14, 06/10/25)",

      "text": "The City shall develop, maintain, and implement land development regulations that serve to \nregulate the form, function, and interplay of land use, development, and associated activities, \nfurther the City’s Comprehensive Plan, and are consistent and compatible with County, State, and \nFederal plans and regulations.",

      "text": "The Planning Department during its review of changes in land use and changes in zoning of \nproperties adjoining single family neighborhoods shall continue its current efforts as provided for \nin the City’s Zoning Code to notify residents, property owners, neighborhood associations, \norganized neighborhood groups and interested parties of upcoming applications and the \nopportunity to provide input.",

      "page_end": 27,
      "text": "Entities requesting changes in land use and zoning for property that adjoins a single-family \nresidential district or neighborhood shall provide ample opportunities for input into the land use \nprocess which may include one or more of the following: additional public notice via regular mail, \nelectronic mail, establishment of website, etc; completion of neighborhood meetings; \nestablishment of point of contact.",

      "page_end": 27,
      "text": "The Planning Department, when receiving a development proposal for property that adjoins a \nsingle-family residential district, shall facilitate the contact and discussion between applicants and \nknown organized neighborhood groups and neighborhood associations to provide the opportunity \nto resolve potential neighborhood issues prior to City review at public hearings. The necessity to \ncomplete further collaboration and consensus decision making to mitigate or resolve identified \nissues may be conducted by the City’s Planning Department or outside mediation services such as \nthe South Florida Regional Planning Council, Institute for Community Collaboration.",

      "text": "The City will continue to monitor septic tank construction, operation, and maintenance, including: \n• Approximate number of fixture units connected. \n• Tank size. \n• Date of original installation, dates of repairs and emptying. \n• Tank location on site. \n• Connection of garbage grinder, dishwasher or washing machine. \n• Drainfield size. \n• Drainfield location on site. \n• Presence of hazardous materials.",

      "text": "Private sanitary sewer collection and pumping systems shall provide annual reports to the City \nregarding their estimated loads and overall conditions of their pumping stations and transmission \nsystems.       "page_start": 43,
      "page_end": 43,
      "text": "The City shall ensure that sanitary sewer facilities are provided to meet projected future demands \nas they are realized, at the required LOS. Facilities to meet new demands shall be provided for by \nthose creating that demand and funded through the sanitary sewer impact fee. Such provision of \nfacilities shall be by construction, payment of impact fees, or taxes, which shall lead to construction, \nor by binding agreement for construction assuring that required facilities are available to meet the \nconcurrency requirements of this plan. Future demand estimates should be used to aid in the sizing \nand scheduling of such facilities, however, construction of facilities need only occur where actual \ndemand is realized, and when such facilities will provide for operation at no less than the LOS \nstandard applicable.       ],
      "page_start": 44,
      "page_end": 44,
      "text": "Water conservation practices utilized in support of the policies in the Natural Resources Element \nshall be employed including maintenance and operation to minimize groundwater and surface \nwater infiltration. Inform the public as to effective use of restricted sanitary sewer plumbing fixtures, \nand participation in MiamiDade programs to improve water conservation. \n \nSolid Waste.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0194",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3."
      ],
      "page_start": 44,
      "page_end": 44,
      "text": "Provide efficient solid waste collection in order to protect the health, safety and environmental \nresources of the community and to maintain the appearance of the City.",

    },
    {

      "heading_path": [

        "Goal COM-3.",

Inform the public as to effective use of restricted sanitary sewer plumbing fixtures, \nand participation in MiamiDade programs to improve water conservation. \n \nSolid Waste.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0194",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3."
      ],
      "page_start": 44,
      "page_end": 44,
      "text": "Provide efficient solid waste collection in order to protect the health, safety and environmental \nresources of the community and to maintain the appearance of the City.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0195",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 44,
      "page_end": 44,
      "text": "Maintain solid waste collection operations in a safe, effective, environmentally sound and efficient \nmanner, in balance with local and regional solid waste comprehensive plan policies. This objective \nshall be achieved through the implementation of the following policies.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0196",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 44,
      "page_end": 44,
      "text": "The City shall be prepared to modify its solid waste collection practices in a manner consistent with \nany new solid waste recycling and hazardous waste practice requirements of the primary agencies \nresponsible for solid waste disposal and recycling.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0197",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 44,
      "page_end": 45,
      "text": "The City shall maintain solid waste collection services at the following LOS: \n• Residential pickup is to be twice a week for household waste; once per week for trash; and \nonce per week for recycling. \n• Commercial service provided by private contract service, shall continue at a level of service \nas agreed upon by the parties, not less than once per week.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0198",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 45,
      "page_end": 45,
      "text": "In cooperation with Miami-Dade County, the City shall provide and maintain a minimum acceptable \nLOS for solid waste collection at an annual average design generation rate of: \n• Five pounds (5 lbs) per capita per day for residential garbage and trash; One half pound (0.5 \nlbs) per capita per day for residential recycling; and \n• Seven pounds (7 lbs) per capita per day for non-residential service. \nCertification of the availability and commitment of capacity by MiamiDade and applicable private \nvendors shall be sufficient to demonstrate that such facilities are available to the site during the \nconcurrency review process.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0199",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 45,
      "page_end": 45,
      "text": "The City shall cooperate in the hazardous waste collection and disposal programs of Miami- Dade \nCounty by enforcing within the City's jurisdiction hazardous waste collection practices required by \nthe county and other agencies with jurisdiction. The City shall coordinate with Miami-Dade County \nDERM in preparation and maintenance of an up-to-date list of all businesses in the City that store, \nuse and/or dispose of hazardous and toxic materials and/or waste.

",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0199",

        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 45,
      "page_end": 45,
      "text": "The City shall cooperate in the hazardous waste collection and disposal programs of Miami- Dade \nCounty by enforcing within the City's jurisdiction hazardous waste collection practices required by \nthe county and other agencies with jurisdiction. The City shall coordinate with Miami-Dade County \nDERM in preparation and maintenance of an up-to-date list of all businesses in the City that store, \nuse and/or dispose of hazardous and toxic materials and/or waste.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0200",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.5."
      ],
      "page_start": 45,
      "page_end": 45,
      "text": "The City shall monitor the general operation of its solid waste collection services to assure the \nminimum acceptable LOS is being maintained. Such a monitoring program shall provide \nrecommendations for needed capital improvements commitments in the Capital Improvements \nBudget and the City’s established Concurrency Management Program.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0201",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-3.",
        "Objective COM-3.1.",
        "Policy COM-3.1.6."
      ],
      "page_start": 45,
      "page_end": 45,
      "text": "The City shall continue to employ water conservation strategies and techniques to minimize the use \nof potable water in the provision of solid waste collection services. Such strategies shall include \nmanagement attention to reducing unattended washdown, self closing nozzles, and wash down \nschedules based upon need and not just time schedule. The City shall continue using recycling \nprocedures for portions of water usage in its solid waste collection services. \n \nDrainage.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0202",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4."
      ],
      "page_start": 45,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "Provide adequate stormwater drainage in order to protect against flood conditions and prevent\ndegradation of quality of receiving waters.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0203",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "Maintain surface and storm water drainage systems in a safe, effective, environmentally sound and \nefficient manner. This objective shall be achieved through the implementation of the following \npolicies.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0204",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "The City should continue to support adequate preventive maintenance programs for drainage \nsystems.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0205",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.2."

This objective shall be achieved through the implementation of the following \npolicies.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0204",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "The City should continue to support adequate preventive maintenance programs for drainage \nsystems.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0205",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "Water conservation, natural resource conservation and related policies will be supported by \ninclusion in positive drain systems of pollution control facilities which will separate oils and greases \nas well as sediment and grit from the discharge waters, as resources permit.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0206",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "Issue development orders only to projects that meet or exceed the minimum acceptable LOS \nstandards for drainage and flood protection as reviewed through the City’s Concurrency \nManagement Program.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0207",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 46,
      "text": "Assist property owners with general information related to flood zone per Federal Emergency \nManagement Agency (FEMA) maps and available floodproofing technology. Flood prone areas \nwhich represent substantial risk for occupants during disaster events should be considered for \ncorrective action or targeted for special attention during disaster response actions.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0208",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.5."
      ],
      "page_start": 46,
      "page_end": 47,
      "text": "The minimum acceptable Flood Protection LOS standards for the City shall be protection from the \ndegree of flooding that would result for a duration of one day from a ten-year storm. All structures \nshall be constructed at, or above, the minimum floor elevation specified in the Flood Insurance Rate \nMaps for Coral Gables in Miami-Dade County, Florida. All new development must retain at least the \nfirst one inch (1\") of storm water runoff onsite, or other nonpublic sites as may be secured for \npermanent services. Designs to meet this first inch criteria will be reviewed for design solutions to\nmeet actual site conditions. The burden for the construction of such facilities shall be borne by the \ndeveloper and/or owner of such sites. Failure of such facilities and subsequent corrections shall also \nbe the responsibility of the developer and/or owner. The City may require greater than the first one \ninch onsite retention where the City establishes more restrictive rules in the public interest.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0209",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.6."

Designs to meet this first inch criteria will be reviewed for design solutions to\nmeet actual site conditions. The burden for the construction of such facilities shall be borne by the \ndeveloper and/or owner of such sites. Failure of such facilities and subsequent corrections shall also \nbe the responsibility of the developer and/or owner. The City may require greater than the first one \ninch onsite retention where the City establishes more restrictive rules in the public interest.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0209",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-4.",
        "Objective COM-4.1.",
        "Policy COM-4.1.6."
      ],
      "page_start": 47,
      "page_end": 47,
      "text": "Promote the use of water conservation measures in stormwater management through the use of \nonsite retention of storm water, use of native vegetation with low water requirements to reduce \nirrigation demands, and community education in water conservation practices in development site \nplanning and drainage design. This policy was revised beyond the EAR recommendations due to \nfurther review. \n \nPotable Water.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0210",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5."
      ],
      "page_start": 47,
      "page_end": 47,
      "text": "The City of Coral Gables shall ensure that a safe potable water supply with sufficient quantity and \nquality to serve the City is available.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0211",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 47,
      "page_end": 47,
      "text": "The potable water treatment and distribution system shall be maintained by the system owner and \noperators in a safe, effective, efficient, environmentally sound and reliable manner consistent with \nthis Comprehensive Plan.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0212",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.1.",
        "Policy COM-5.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 47,
      "page_end": 48,
      "text": "The minimum acceptable LOS standards of potable water shall be 155 gallons per day per capita \nand such water is to be delivered to users at a pressure of not less than twenty pounds per square \ninch (psi) and not greater than one-hundred (100) psi. The regional treatment system shall operate \nwith a maximum daily rated capacity which is no less than two (2%) percent above the maximum \nday daily flow for the preceding year and an annual average daily capacity two (2%) percent above \nthe average daily system demand for the preceding 5 years. Water quality shall meet or exceed all \nfederal, state, and County primary standards for potable water; and system wide storage capacity \nfor finished water shall equal no less than fifteen (15%) percent of the Countywide average daily \ndemand.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0213",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.1.",
        "Policy COM-5.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 48,
      "page_end": 48,
      "text": "The minimum acceptable Level of Service standards for fire flows shall be maintained at not less \nthan: \n• 500 gpm in single-family residential areas of densities of less than 5.8 units per acre; \n• 750 gpm for single-family and duplex residential areas at densities of 5.8 dwelling units per \nacre or more; \n• 1500 gpm in multifamily residential and low intensity commercial areas of two floors or less; \nand \n• 3000 gpm in all other commercial and industrial areas.

",
        "Objective COM-5.1.",
        "Policy COM-5.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 48,
      "page_end": 48,
      "text": "The minimum acceptable Level of Service standards for fire flows shall be maintained at not less \nthan: \n• 500 gpm in single-family residential areas of densities of less than 5.8 units per acre; \n• 750 gpm for single-family and duplex residential areas at densities of 5.8 dwelling units per \nacre or more; \n• 1500 gpm in multifamily residential and low intensity commercial areas of two floors or less; \nand \n• 3000 gpm in all other commercial and industrial areas. \nAutomatic fire suppression systems shall be required in all buildings of six floors or more.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0214",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.1.",
        "Policy COM-5.1.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 48,
      "page_end": 48,
      "text": "The City shall seek to provide adequate water distribution and hydrants for all existing and new \nareas annexed and serviced by the Fire Department. All existing and new water distribution \nsystems, fire hydrants and flows shall be in compliance with the National Fire Protection Standards \n(NFPA) and Insurance Services Office (ISO) requirements, as amended.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0215",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.1.",
        "Policy COM-5.1.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 48,
      "page_end": 48,
      "text": "Water conservation practices, strategies and techniques shall be utilized to minimize the waste and \nunnecessary degradation of potable water sources and supplies and support the policies in the \nNatural Resources Element. The use of water efficient plumbing fixtures and public education in \nwater conservation methods are to be continued by the City.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0216",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 48,
      "page_end": 48,
      "text": "The City of Coral Gables shall comply with its 10-year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan, as required \nby section 163.3177(6)(c), F.S.. The Work Plan will be updated, at a minimum, every 5 years. The City \nof Coral Gables Water Supply Facilities Work Plan is designed to: assess current and projected \npotable water demands; evaluate the sources and capacities of available water supplies; and, \nidentify those water supply projects, using all available technologies, necessary to meet the City’s \nwater demands for a 10-year period.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0217",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2.",
        "Policy COM-5.2.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 48,
      "page_end": 49,
      "text": "Comply with the 10-year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan and incorporate such work plan into the \nCoral Gables Comprehensive Plan.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0218",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2.",
        "Policy COM-5.2.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 49,
      "text": "Coordinate appropriate aspects of the City’s Comprehensive Plan with the South Florida Water \nManagement District’s regional water supply plan adopted February 15, 2007 and with the Miami-\nDade County 20-Year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan adopted April 24, 2008.

",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0218",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2.",
        "Policy COM-5.2.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 49,
      "text": "Coordinate appropriate aspects of the City’s Comprehensive Plan with the South Florida Water \nManagement District’s regional water supply plan adopted February 15, 2007 and with the Miami-\nDade County 20-Year Water Supply Facilities Work Plan adopted April 24, 2008. The City shall \namend its Comprehensive Plan and Work Plan as required to provide consistency with the District \nand County plans.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0219",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2.",
        "Policy COM-5.2.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 49,
      "text": "The City shall coordinate the planning of potable water and sanitary sewer facilities and services \nand LOS standards within the Miami-Dade County Water and Sewer Department, DERM, the South \nFlorida Water Management District, and the Lower East Coast Water Supply Plan Update.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0220",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2.",
        "Policy COM-5.2.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 49,
      "text": "The City shall coordinate with Miami-Dade County WASD by requiring applications to be reviewed \nby WASD during the site plan review process prior to approving a building permit, in order to \ndetermine whether adequate water supplies will be available to serve the development by the \nanticipated issuance date of the certificate of occupancy for properties located within the City. \nAdditional coordination efforts will occur between WASD and the City through the water allocation \nsystem. Monthly building permit data will be provided to MDWASD to track development activity \nwithin the City. The City will monitor proposed amendments to the Miami-Dade County \nComprehensive Development Master Plan as they relate to water supply planning in the South \nMiami area and provide input as necessary.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0221",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-5.",
        "Objective COM-5.2.",
        "Policy COM-5.2.5."
      ],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 49,
      "text": "The City Planning Director or a representative will attend the Miami-Dade Planners Technical \nCommittee meeting or other County technical planners meeting to share information regarding \nwater supply needs and coordinate water use issues as needed. The Planners Technical Committee \nis a council of professional planners representing local governments and public regulatory/review \nagencies in Miami-Dade County that addresses common concerns and shares resources toward \nsolving planning problems. \n \nNatural Ground Water Aquifer Recharge.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0222",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-6."
      ],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "The functions of natural groundwater aquifer recharge areas within the City shall be protected and \nmaintained.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0223",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-6.",
        "Objective COM-6.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 50,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "Manage the natural ground water aquifer recharge conditions in a safe, effective and reliable \nmanner as required by current design standards and codes. This objective shall be achieved \nthrough the implementation of the following policies.

],
      "page_start": 49,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "The functions of natural groundwater aquifer recharge areas within the City shall be protected and \nmaintained.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0223",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-6.",
        "Objective COM-6.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 50,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "Manage the natural ground water aquifer recharge conditions in a safe, effective and reliable \nmanner as required by current design standards and codes. This objective shall be achieved \nthrough the implementation of the following policies.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0224",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-6.",
        "Objective COM-6.1.",
        "Policy COM-6.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 50,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "Encourage improved groundwater recharge by requiring all new construction projects to consider \nproviding: \n• Greater pervious open and green space. \n• Pervious pavements. \n• French drains, slabcovered trenches or drainage wells, and limit overflows. \n• Allow direct overland flow discharge to surface waters (canals or bay) only when no other \npractical or effective method of storm water discharge is possible. \n• Allow positive drainage discharges to surface waters only when other methods are \nimpractical or impossible, and only when adequate pollution control (grit and grease) is \nprovided.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0225",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-6.",
        "Objective COM-6.1.",
        "Policy COM-6.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 50,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "Encourage designs which will diminish groundwater withdrawals and increase high quality \ngroundwater recharge. This policy was revised beyond the EAR recommendations due to further \nreview.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0226",
      "heading_path": [
        "Community Facilities Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal COM-6.",
        "Objective COM-6.1.",
        "Policy COM-6.1.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 50,
      "page_end": 50,
      "text": "Comply with SFWMD and Miami-Dade County Code and environmental protection rules for storm \nwater disposal methods. Refer to the LOS for drainage for retention standards to be met.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0227",
      "heading_path": [
        "Housing Element"
      ],

      "text": "The City is essentially built out and is characterized by extraordinarily high land values, significant \naddition to the affordable housing inventory is highly unlikely. However, the City is committed to \nthe following directed courses of action to improve affordable housing supply on a local and \nregion-wide basis: \n• Pursuant to Miami-Dade County Resolution 1477-96, the City of Coral Gables is a participant \non the Miami-Dade County Infill Strategy Task Force. This Task Force is directed towards \nidentifying strategies for infill, redevelopment, and County-wide affordable housing \ninitiatives, including regulatory, financial, and design strategies for implementation. \n• The City of Coral Gables is working in partnership with the City of Miami to develop \nadditional affordable housing through the City of Miami Community Development Block \nGrant program. This partnership has been responsible for the addition of seventeen (17) \nhousing units to the Coral Gables affordable housing inventory. \n• The City of Coral Gables shall continue to participate in the South Florida Regional Planning \nCouncils affordable housing initiatives. \n• The City has a commitment from an approved, permitted development project to provide 35 \nrental affordable/attainable housing units within the mixed use area of the City.",

      "text": "The City shall coordinate new residential development with the future availability of public school \nfacilitiesconsistent with the adopted LOS standards for public school concurrency, to ensure the \ninclusion of those projects necessary to address existing deficiencies in the 5-year schedule of \ncapital improvements, and meet future needs based upon achieving and maintaining the adopted \nLOS standards throughout the planning period.",

      ],
      "page_start": 60,
      "page_end": 60,
      "text": "Beginning January 1, 2008, the adopted LOS standard for all public school facilities within and \nserved by the City of Coral Gables is 100% utilization of Florida Inventory of School Houses (FISH) \nCapacity (With Relocatable Classrooms). This LOS standard, except for magnet schools, shall be \napplicable in each public school Concurrency Service Area (CSA), defined as the public school \nattendance boundary established by Miami-Dade County Public Schools. The adopted LOS \nstandard for Magnet Schools is 100% of FISH (With Relocatable Classrooms), which shall be \ncalculated on a district wide basis.",
      "tables": []

      "page_start": 60,
      "page_end": 61,
      "text": "Although not the established LOS standard, it is the goal of Miami-Dade County Public Schools and \nthe City for all public school facilities to achieve 100% utilization of Permanent FISH (No \nRelocatable Classrooms) capacity by January 1, 2018. To help achieve the desired 100% utilization \nof Permanent FISH by 2018, Miami-Dade County Public Schools should continue to decrease the \nnumber of relocatable classrooms over time. Public school facilities that achieve 100% utilization of \nPermanent FISH capacity should, to the extent possible, no longer utilize relocatable classrooms, \nexcept as an operational solution to achieve the LOS standard during replacement, remodeling, \nrenovation or expansion of a public school facility. However, the LOS standard for concurrency \npurposes remains as established above. \n(Ord. No. 2025-14, 06/10/25)",

      "text": "In the event the adopted LOS standard of a CSA cannot be met as a result of a proposed \ndevelopment’s impact, the development may proceed, provided at least one of the following \noptions is satisfied: \n• The development’s impact can be shifted to one or more contiguous CSAs that have \navailable capacity and is located, either in whole or in part, within the same Miami-Dade \nCounty Public Schools designated geographic areas (Northwest, Northeast, Southwest, or \nSoutheast) as the proposed development; or, \n• The development’s impact is mitigated, proportionate to the demand for public schools it \ncreated, pursuant to a Proportionate Share Mitigation Agreement through a combination of \none or more appropriate proportionate share mitigation options, as defined in Section",

      "text": "The minimum or lowest quality acceptable peakperiod* operating LOS standards for State Principal 
Arterial, Minor Arterial, County Minor Arterial, County and City Collector roads within the City shall 
be the minimum acceptable peakperiod LOS standard: 
• Where public transit service does not exist, roadways shall operate at or above LOS E; within 
the Special Transportation Area (STA) twenty (20%) percent of nonState roads may operate 
below LOS E. All County roads within the STA will maintain LOS standards consistent with the 
County adopted standards. 
• Where public transit service having headways of twenty (20) minutes or less is provided 
within 1/2 mile distance, roadways shall operate at no greater than one-hundred twenty 
(120%) percent of their capacity; 
• Where commuter rail or express bus public transit service exists, generally parallel roads 
within ½ mile shall operate at no greater than one-hundred fifty (150%) percent of their 
capacity. 
* Peak period means the average of the two highest consecutive hours of traffic volume during a 
weekday.",

      "text": "As a vibrant mature City located in rapidly growing Miami-Dade County, the City shall continue to \npursue and promote infill and redevelopment in appropriate parts of the City, especially within the \nCity’s GRID. The City shall research the following: \n• The possible expansion and upgrade of the current trolley system to other destinations \nwithin the City which may include a northern extension beyond 8th Street and connection to \nthe University of Miami campus. \n• Potential development incentives and/or economic incentives to promote trolley ridership. \n• Maintain the existing Coral Gables Mediterranean Style Design Standards, which awards \ndensity and height bonuses for developments which provide pedestrian amenities thereby \nencouraging walkability.",

      "text": "The City shall, as a part of its development review process, continue to maximize utilization of \nexisting roadway capacity and reduce peak period congestion by implementing to the maximum \nextent feasible, traffic operation improvements and transportation systems management \nalternatives including but not limited to the following: \n• Limitations of the number and width of vehicular driveways/curbcuts on streets to minimize \npedestrian intrusion/obstacles. \n• Improved signal timing. \n• Intersection signing, markings, channelization.\n• Restrictions and management of onstreet parking.

      "text": "The City shall, as a part of its development review process, continue to maximize utilization of \nexisting roadway capacity and reduce peak period congestion by implementing to the maximum \nextent feasible, traffic operation improvements and transportation systems management \nalternatives including but not limited to the following: \n• Limitations of the number and width of vehicular driveways/curbcuts on streets to minimize \npedestrian intrusion/obstacles. \n• Improved signal timing. \n• Intersection signing, markings, channelization.\n• Restrictions and management of onstreet parking. \n• The use of mass transit and paratransit services. \n• Possible expansion of routes of the existing trolley system. \n• Continue improvements of the existing trolley system (i.e., additional cars). \n• Employerbased van pooling, car pooling. \n• Employerbased staggered and/or flexible work hours. \n• Provisions for the accommodation of bicycles and associated bicycle support facilities.",

      "page_end": 87,
      "text": "Ensure the preservation of trees during development or redevelopment wherever possible, and \nconsistent with the tree preservation ordinance and landscape ordinance. Where trees approved for \nremoval as a last resort, require that they be replaced with quality trees of equal or greater canopy.",

    {

      "page_start": 87,
      "page_end": 87,
      "text": "The City shall conserve, manage, use and protect natural and environmental resources and maintain \nand enhance the natural balance of ecological functions in the coastal area.",

      "heading_path": [

        "Objective NAT-2.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 87,
      "page_end": 88,
      "text": "Maintain or improve coastal area and estuarine environmental quality, as measured by existing \nbaseline environmental indicators for water quality provided by Miami-Dade Department of\nEnvironmental Regulation and Management. This objective shall be achieved through the \nimplementation of the following policies.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {

      "heading_path": [

        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",

        "Objective NAT-2.1.",
        "Policy NAT-2.1.1."
      ],

      "page_end": 88,

      "heading_path": [

        "Objective NAT-2.1.",
        "Policy NAT-2.1.2."
      ],

      "page_end": 88,

    },
    {

      "heading_path": [
        "Natural Resources Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",

        "Objective NAT-2.1.",
        "Policy NAT-2.1.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 88,
      "page_end": 88,
      "text": "The City shall cooperate with the South Florida Water Management District, state agencies, and \nlocal government jurisdictions for areawide water resources planning and management.",

    },

      "heading_path": [

        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",

        "Policy NAT-2.1.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 88,
      "page_end": 88,

",

      ],

      "page_end": 89,
      "text": "Coordinate with appropriate public agencies for the management of the coastal zone to provide a \nbalance between irreversible commitments and conservation of resources.     },

        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",

        "Policy NAT-2.2.2."
      ],

      ],

      "text": "Restore and enhance disturbed or degraded natural resources and implement programs to \nmitigate future natural resources disruption or degradation in the coastal area. This objective shall \nbe achieved through the implementation of the following policies.",

        "Policy NAT-2.3.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 89,
      "page_end": 89,
      "text": "Existing coastal wetlands and submerged lands should not be drained or filled, and should be \nrestored or enhanced where disturbed or degraded by development. The City shall monitor dredge \nand fill permits issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and shall further monitor new \ndevelopment applications to the City to ensure that this policy is enforced.",

        "Policy NAT-2.3.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 89,
      "page_end": 90,
      "text": "Specific and cumulative impacts of development or redevelopment upon wetlands; water quality,\nwater quantity, wildlife habitat, living marine resources, and shoreline systems shall be limited by \nstrictly regulating land alteration activities likely to result in erosion and sedimentation, or longterm \nwater quality degradation and habitat loss.",

        "Policy NAT-2.3.3."
      ],

      "page_end": 90,
      "text": "Protect existing natural shoreline areas, establish construction standards which minimize the impact \nof manmade structures on shoreline systems, and restore altered shorelines within the City's \njurisdiction.

",
      "tables": []
    },

      ],
      "page_start": 90,
      "page_end": 90,
      "text": "The functions of natural groundwater aquifer recharge areas within the City shall be protected and \nmaintained.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0457",
      "heading_path": [
        "Natural Resources Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal NAT-3.",
        "Objective NAT-3.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 90,
      "page_end": 90,
      "text": "Manage the natural ground water aquifer recharge conditions in a safe, effective and reliable \nmanner as required by current design standards and codes.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0458",
      "heading_path": [
        "Natural Resources Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal NAT-3.",
        "Objective NAT-3.1.",
        "Policy NAT-3.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 90,
      "page_end": 90,
      "text": "Encourage improved groundwater recharge by requiring all new construction projects to consider \nproviding the following \n• Greater pervious open and green space. \n• Pervious pavements. \n• French drains, slab covered trenches or drainage wells, and limit overflows. \n• Allow direct overland flow discharge to surface waters (canals or bay) only when no other \npractical or effective method of storm water discharge is possible. \nAllow positive drainage discharges to surface waters only when other methods are impractical or \nimpossible, and only when adequate pollution control (grit and grease) is provided.",

        "Policy NAT-3.1.2."
      ],

      ],
      "page_start": 91,
      "page_end": 91,
      "text": "The City of Coral Gables recreation system will serve the residents with neighborhood parks and \nopen spaces that offer both passive and active recreation activities and facilities; that are linked \ntogether with a network of sidewalks, pathways and bike lanes; and provide public/open spaces \nthat serve as gathering places in the downtown area.",

    {
      "section_id": "s0464",
      "heading_path": [
        "Recreation and Open Space Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal REC-1.",
        "Objective REC-1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 91,
      "page_end": 91,
      "text": "Provide quality recreation programs and adequate provision of recreation facilities to meet the \nneeds of residents.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0465",
      "heading_path": [
        "Recreation and Open Space Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal REC-1.",
        "Objective REC-1.1.",
        "Policy REC-1.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 91,
      "page_end": 93,
      "text": "Maintain the existing level of services (LOS) provided by recreation programs and activities to meet \nthe continuing needs of all residents. The minimum acceptable LOS standards for recreation and \nopen space facilities will be measured by the following radius standards. \n \n \nRecreation facilities radius standard:\nRecreation facilities radius standard: \nPark Type \nAcreage/Mileage \nService Radius \nUrban Open Spaces \n0 - .25 \n5 minute walk or 0 .25 \nmiles \nNeighborhood Park \n.25 - 3 \n10 minute walk or 0.5 \nmiles \nCommunity Facilities \n3 – 100 \n15 minute drive or 5 miles \nBeach/Waterway Access \nN/A \n20 minute drive or 6.7 \nmiles \nNon-City District/Regional \nVaries \n30 minute drive or 10 \nmiles \nTrail Ways \nAt least 100’ in \nlength \n10 minute walk or 0.5 \nmiles \nPrivate Park/ Recreation \nFacilities \nVaries \n10 minute drive or 3.3 \nmiles \n \nUrban Open Space are those designated areas which are between 0 and .25 acres and typically \ncontain landscaped areas but have very limited or no facilities or other improvement. The \nrecreational use of these sites is limited by their location and/or size. These sites serve to preserve \nthe aesthetic quality of an area or to intersperse congested urban environments with aesthetically \npleasing buffer areas.

The \nrecreational use of these sites is limited by their location and/or size. These sites serve to preserve \nthe aesthetic quality of an area or to intersperse congested urban environments with aesthetically \npleasing buffer areas. Some open space areas may serve as linear parks, vest pocket parks, while \nother areas are parkways, boulevard medians, plazas, malls, courthouse squares and promenades \nSee REC-1: Level of Service Map. \n \nNeighborhood Parks are those designated areas that are “walk-to” facilities where residents may\nwalk or bicycle within a given neighborhood. Areas for diverse recreational activities which may \ninclude, but are not limited to the following: field games; court games; sports fields; playground \napparatus area; picnic area; landscaping and garden areas; and senior citizen areas. The \nNeighborhood Park is a place where neighbors and their families go to meetSee REC-1: Level of \nService Map. \n \nCommunity Facilities is an area that provides a diverse range of recreational and leisure activities or \nprovides very specific active recreation facilities for all individuals and families. Facilities and \nactivities may include, but are not limited to athletic fields, swimming pools, gymnasiums, \nperforming and community centers. These facilities are designed to meet the recreation needs of \nthe entire community See REC-1: Level of Service Map. \n \nNon-City District/Regional Parks is an area selected for its natural and ornamental quality and its \nsuitability of which the purpose is to function as a regionally-based recreational activities area at \nnon-city properties. Recreational activities could include, but not be limited to, swimming, \npicnicking, camping, boating, fishing, and a variety of trail uses See Rec -1 Level of Service Map .",
      "tables": []
    },

      "text": "Continue to identify existing recreation facilities needs in the five (5) year capital improvements \nschedule for the Recreation Department, and correct or improve deficiencies as funding becomes \navailable.       "text": "The City shall maintain existing recreation land and facilities through the use of proper \nmanagement and funding techniques. This shall be partially achieved by continuing efforts toward collecting, \nmaintaining, and updating data concerning public and private resource inventory, recreation \nimprovements, and demand factors, and by improving design criteria and evaluation to attain a \nhigh quality park and recreation system.       ],
      "page_start": 105,
      "page_end": 106,
      "text": "The City shall seek to reduce the exposure of life and property to hurricanes and other disasters \nthrough the planning and implementation of emergency preparedness, response and recovery \nplans.",

    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0541",

        "Policy SAF-1.4.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 106,
      "page_end": 106,
      "text": "Develop an emergency preparedness, response and recovery plan and update it every two years to \nprovide comprehensive pre-disaster planning consistent with Miami-Dade County’s Emergency \nManagement Plan.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0542",

        "Policy SAF-1.4.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 106,
      "page_end": 106,
      "text": "Due to the City’s location within the Coastal High Hazard Area and general vulnerability to \nhurricane events, the City shall implement and/or adhere to emergency management and hurricane \nevacuation plans and procedures through land use controls.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {

        "Policy SAF-1.4.3."
      ],

      "page_end": 106,
      "text": "The City shall coordinate with adjacent municipalities, Miami-Dade County, the Florida Department \nof Transportation and other agencies, as appropriate, to ensure the ability of the regional \ntransportation network to provide for the safe and timely evacuation of residents in a hurricane or \nother emergency event.",

      "page_end": 106,
      "text": "Protect human life and investment in the coastal area of the City.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0547",
      "heading_path": [
        "Public Safety Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal SAF-2.",
        "Objective SAF-2.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 106,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "Limit public expenditures in coastal areas to projects clearly in the public interest and which \nminimize the risk from storm damage. This objective shall be achieved through the implementation \nof the following policies.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0548",
      "heading_path": [
        "Public Safety Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal SAF-2.",
        "Objective SAF-2.1.",
        "Policy SAF-2.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 107,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "Public expenditures for infrastructure improvements shall be located outside flood prone areas, to \nthe extent practicable, to keep floodways as unobstructed as possible.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0549",
      "heading_path": [
        "Public Safety Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal SAF-2.",
        "Objective SAF-2.1.",
        "Policy SAF-2.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 107,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "Limit public expenditures that subsidize development permitted in coastal areas as defined herein \nexcept for restoration or enhancement of natural resources.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0550",
      "heading_path": [
        "Public Safety Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal SAF-2.",
        "Objective SAF-2.1.",
        "Policy SAF-2.1.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 107,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "The City shall abide by the Coastal High Hazard Area (CHHA) defined as the area below the \nelevation of the category 1 storm surge line as established by a Sea, Lake, and Overland Surges \nfrom Hurricanes (SLOSH) computerized storm surge model (see SAF-1: Storm Tide Atlas Map).",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0551",
      "heading_path": [
        "Public Safety Element",
        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal SAF-2.",
        "Objective SAF-2.1.",
        "Policy SAF-2.1.4."
      ],
      "page_start": 107,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "The Coastal Area within the City of Coral Gables shall be defined as the land south of the Coral \nGables Waterway, east of Old Cutler Road, and north of the southern limit of the City.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0552",

",

      ],
      "page_start": 107,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "The Coastal Area within the City of Coral Gables shall be defined as the land south of the Coral \nGables Waterway, east of Old Cutler Road, and north of the southern limit of the City.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {
      "section_id": "s0552",

        "Goals, Objectives and Policies:",
        "Goal SAF-2.",
        "Objective SAF-2.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 107,
      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "Assure that future development or redevelopment maintains or reduces hurricane evacuation \ntimes. The City establishes an out-of-county hurricane evacuation time for a category 5 hurricane of \n16 hours. Mitigation is permitted to achieve and maintain these standards.",
      "tables": []
    },
    {

        "Policy SAF-2.2.1."
      ],

      "page_end": 107,
      "text": "Manage the location of population concentration by maintaining lowdensity residential land use \ndesignations in the CHHA by directing higherdensity population concentrations to areas away from \nthe CHHA through the City's land use planning process.",

      ],

      "text": "Monitor hurricane and emergency management studies with the intent of identifying and \ncorrecting deficiencies. Continue to integrate regional and local notification and evacuation \nprocedures into the City’s Emergency Operations Plan.",

        "Objective SAF-2.3."
      ],
      "page_start": 108,
      "page_end": 108,
      "text": "Establish priorities and development guidelines for postdisaster redevelopment in the coastal area.",
      "tables": []

    {

        "Policy SAF-2.3.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 108,
      "page_end": 108,
      "text": "Update the Post Disaster Development Plan annually. The plan shall address land use, public safety, \ninfrastructure, and public investment concerns. The plan shall include policies to distinguish \nbetween immediate repair and cleanup actions needed to protect public health and safety and \nlongterm repair and redevelopment activities; and the removal, relocation, or structural \nmodification of damaged infrastructure and unsafe structures. The plan should also ensure all \nredevelopment shall reduce or eliminate the exposure of human life and public and private \nproperty to natural hazards.",
      "tables": []
    },

      ],

      "page_end": 108,
      "text": "Provide for increased public access to the shoreline consistent with public needs, continuing and \nreplacing adequate physical public access to shorelines; enforcing the public access requirements \nof the Coastal Zone Protection Act of 1985, as amended, and providing transportation or parking \nfacilities for shoreline access.",

    {

        "Objective SAF-2.4.",
        "Policy SAF-2.4.2."
      ],

      "page_end": 109,
      "text": "Utilize interlocal agreements or other methods for coordinating with Miami-Dade County and \naffected adjacent local governments to complete the following: ensure adequate sites exist for \nwaterdependent uses; reduce exposure to natural hazards; and ensure public shoreline access is \nmaintained.",

    },
    {

        "Objective SAF-2.4.",
        "Policy SAF-2.4.3."

    },

        "Policy SAF-2.4.4."
      ],

      "page_end": 109,
      "text": "In evaluating applications for marinas or marina siting all of the following shall be addressed: land \nuse compatibility; availability of upland support services; existing protective status or ownership; \nhurricane contingency planning; protection of water quality; water depth; environmental \ndisruptions and mitigation actions; availability for public use; and, economic need and feasibility. \nThe criteria shall be reviewed by the Planning Department on an annual basis and updated as \nnecessary.",

      "text": "Ensure that required infrastructure is available to serve the development or redevelopment at \ndensities proposed by the future land use plan in the coastal area, consistent with coastal resource \nprotection and safe evacuation. Funding for infrastructure shall be phased to coincide with the \ndemands generated by development or redevelopment. Infrastructure shall not be made available \nunless the development or redevelopment meets the requirements of the Concurrency \nManagement System.",

      ],
      "page_start": 110,
      "page_end": 110,
      "text": "In reviewing applications for shoreline development, first priority shall be directed to the following \nshoreline uses: \n• Non-structural shoreline protection uses such as native shoreline revegetation programs. \n• Approved water-dependent shoreline uses such as pile supported access ways and duly \npermitted dock facilities. All such facilities shall satisfy all applicable county, state and federal \nregulations and all provisions of the City's Zoning Code and all requisite permits from all \nenvironmental permitting agencies prior to obtaining City approval. \nSecond priority shall be directed toward uses such as: \n• Parking facilities for shoreline access located outside wetlands. \n• Residential structures that comply with building codes for structures within the coastal \nbuilding zone. \n• Recreational facilities which comply with applicable codes.",

Urban Open Spaces are those designated areas which are between 0 and .25 acres and typically 
contain landscaped areas but have very limited or no facilities or other improvements. The 
recreational use of these sites is limited by their location and/or size. These sites serve to preserve 
the aesthetic quality of an area or to intersperse congested urban environments with aesthetically 
pleasing buffer areas. Some open space areas may serve as linear parks or vest pocket parks, while 
other areas are parkways, boulevard medians, plazas, malls, courthouse squares and promenades. 
 
Neighborhood Parks those designated areas that are “walk-to” facilities where residents may walk 
or bicycle to the park within a given neighborhood. Areas for diverse recreational activities which 
may include, but are not limited to the following: field games; court games; sports fields; 
playground apparatus area; picnic area; landscaping and gardens areas; and senior citizen areas. 
The Neighborhood Park is a place where neighbors and their families go to meet.

activities may include, but are not limited to athletic fields, swimming pools, gymnasiums,

the entire community.

public school facilities consistent with the adopted level of service (LOS) standards for public school 
concurrency to ensure the inclusion of those projects necessary to address existing deficiencies in 
the 5-year schedule of capital improvements, and meet future needs based upon achieving and 
maintaining the adopted level of service standards throughout the planning period. Beginning 
January 1, 2008, the adopted LOS standard for all Miami-Dade County Public Schools facilities is 
100% utilization of Florida Inventory of School Houses (FISH) Capacity (with relocatable

      "page_start": 124,
      "page_end": 124,
      "text": "The City of Coral Gables will take measurable steps towards becoming a “sustainable” community \nby providing a healthy setting for residents, workers, property owners and visitors and increase \nawareness of green development practices and ways to have a significant impact on the City’s \nenvironment including the following: protecting the quality of air, water, land and other natural \nresources; conserving native vegetation, fish, wildlife and worldwide ecosystems; minimize the \ncarbon footprint; and reduce greenhouse emissions. \n \nGeneral",
      "tables": []

        "Goal GRN-1.",
        "Objective GRN-1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 124,
      "page_end": 125,
      "text": "The City shall continue its current efforts to be recognized as a “green” and “sustainable” \ncommunity through participation in public and private partnerships/programs which may include \nany of the following: \n• Other local governments, the state and the federal government. \n• South Florida Water Management District and Florida Department of Environmental \nProtection Conserve Florida Program. \n• Florida Green Building Coalition, Inc. to establish and maintain a Florida system of statewide \ngreen building standards and third party certification programs with economic and \nenvironmental benefits. \n• Florida friendly landscaping. \n• Florida Green Lodging to designate lodging establishments as “green” for following \nenvironmentally sensitive operating procedures. \n• Florida Solar Energy Systems Incentives Program providing for rebates for the installation of \nqualified solar energy systems. \n• Florida Water Star Program, a third party certification program offered by the Water \nManagement District for water efficiency in household appliances, plumbing fixtures, \nirrigation systems and landscapes. \n• University of Florida Extension Service Program, Florida Yard and Neighborhoods which \nencourages homeowners and professionals to create and maintain Florida friendly \nlandscaping that protects the natural environment. \n• Green Building Initiative, not for profit organization whose mission is to accelerate the\nadoption of building practices that result in energy efficient, healthier and environmental \nsustainable buildings.",

      "text": "The City will actively participate and partner with the Florida Department of Transportation, the \nMiami-Dade MPO, the Miami-Dade Transit Authority and the South Florida Regional Planning \nCouncil to consider additional opportunities to reduce the negative impact transportation uses \nhave on the environment.",

      "text": "The City will encourage and collaborate with private parking facility operators to allign pricing \nstrategies and policies, with municipal garage rates. This initiative aims to reduce vehicle idling and \ncongestion caused by drivers circling in search of on-street parking. By encouraging drivers to \nutilize oﬀ-street garages, the City seeks to decrease traﬃc congestion, improve air quality, and \nenhance mobility eﬃciency within its urban core. The City will identify at least three parking \nfacilities to enter into discussions with as it relates to this policy. To encourage this policy, the City \nshall conduct the following: \n1. Engage Stakeholders: Identify and collaborate with at least three (3) private parking facilities \nannually to discuss pricing harmonization strategies and sustainable parking solutions. \n2. Pilot Projects: Establish at least one (1) pilot program by 2035 in collaboration with a private\nparking operator to evaluate the eﬀectiveness of pricing parity on traﬃc patterns, air quality, \nand parking utilization rates. \n3. Incentivize Participation: Explore incentives, such as tax benefits or public recognition \nprograms, to encourage private operators to adopt pricing strategies aligned with the City’s \ngoals. \nBy integrating value-pricing policies and harmonizing garage rates, the City reaﬃrms its \ncommitment to sustainable transportation and reducing the environmental impact of urban \nmobility. \n(Ord.       "page_end": 133,
      "text": "Maintain, protect, and enhance the quality of life and appearance of Coral Gables’ Coastal Zone \nincluding the preservation of natural resources, restoration of valuable natural resources, and \nenhancement of the built environment.",

      ],
      "page_start": 133,
      "page_end": 133,
      "text": "Preserve and restore existing natural systems resources including wetlands and mangrove systems \nwithin Matheson Hammock Park, Chapman Field Park, R. Hardy Matheson Preserve, and the \nCocoplum mangrove preserve, as well as those portions of Biscayne Bay that lie within the City's \nboundaries.",

    {

        "Goal CMT-1.",
        "Objective CMT-1.1.",
        "Policy CMT-1.1.1."
      ],
      "page_start": 133,
      "page_end": 133,
      "text": "The City will adhere to Miami-Dade County Regulatory and Economic Resources Department – \nDivision of Environmental Resources Management (RER-DERM) standards and require RER-DERM \napprovals in its permitting procedures to ensure that facilities in the Coastal Zone as defined in \nChapter 380.205(2) F.S. and near major canals do not pose a significant threat to water quality or \ndiminish the quality or extent of the natural environment.",

    },

        "Policy CMT-1.1.2."
      ],
      "page_start": 133,
      "page_end": 134,
      "text": "Identify and reduce point and non-point sources of pollution into Biscayne Bay and its adjacent \ntributaries within the City through coordination with Miami-Dade County RER-DERM, the South\nFlorida Water Management District, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and any other appropriate \nstate and federal agencies and entities, in order to reduce pollution, improve water quality in \nBiscayne Bay and waterways within the City limits and jurisdiction, into Biscayne Bay.",

],

      "text": "Identify and reduce point and non-point sources of pollution into Biscayne Bay and its adjacent \ntributaries within the City through coordination with Miami-Dade County RER-DERM, the South\nFlorida Water Management District, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and any other appropriate \nstate and federal agencies and entities, in order to reduce pollution, improve water quality in \nBiscayne Bay and waterways within the City limits and jurisdiction, into Biscayne Bay.",

      "page_end": 134,
      "text": "Site development criteria will ensure that development or redevelopment within the Coastal Zone \nwill not adversely affect or diminish the natural environment or lead to a net loss of public access to \nthe City's natural resources.",

        "Policy CMT-1.1.5."
      ],

      "page_end": 134,
